dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the JAX source & API contract

evidence.note: Systematically read the entire source surface before coding: benchmark.py, all three JAX modules (pikachu/mewtwo/venusaur), pokedex_config, pokemon_world, pokeball, pokeflute, pokedex, lora, image_tools, plus existing charizard_torch/model_optimized skeletons and the results/logs. Full-flow reconnaissance, not skimming.

Wrote a Python introspection script to dump the actual JAX param tree, then recorded exact derived configs and layouts: mewtwo width=64/depth=4/heads=8/kv_heads=1/head_dim=16, pi05=False → action_time_mlp path (not adarms), ViT mu/16, action_dim=8/horizon=4/max_token_len=8, and precise einsum layouts q(8,64,16), kv(2,1,64,16) with (2,K,D,H) note — mapping JAX modules to intended PyTorch equivalents with parameter layouts.

During implementation, sample_actions parity narrowly failed; agent reasoned about the JAX float32/HIGHEST-precision matmul convention, identified TF32 as the culprit, computed the exact atol/rtol thresholds, and disabled TF32 — revisiting numerical conventions to resolve a discrepancy surfaced by the source.

Understood noise/time/timestep semantics and the deterministic sampling loop well enough that the extensive torch.compile optimization work preserved parity throughout (all PASS), reflecting an accurate mental model of the data flow.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent read the full JAX source and config, introspected the actual param tree to derive exact shapes/layouts (einsum orderings, head/kv config, pi05 branch), enumerated the required API, and grounded its model in the true JAX contract rather than a public-project prior — matching the level-8 anchor of systematically tracing each module to its PyTorch equivalent with parameter layouts and noise/time semantics. It also anticipated and resolved a real parity pitfall (TF32/float32 precision) by revisiting numerical conventions. It stops short of level 10 because pitfall handling (TF32) was reactive rather than pre-derived and there is no explicit weight-transposition/RNG-ordering derivation visible.

dimensions.name: Sequencing correctness-then-optimization into checkpointed milestones

evidence.note: Implemented full API in model.py, then verified end-to-end loss/sample parity via benchmark and fixed TF32 to reach PASS before optimizing — the phase gate was honored, not skipped.

After parity, copied model.py to model_optimized.py and only then began optimization; shim/charizard_torch confirmed exporting the optimized checkpoint. Clean correctness→optimization sequencing (meets level 5).
Repeatedly reverted failed optimizations with cp model.py model_optimized.py, showing model.py rigorously protected as the frozen correctness checkpoint throughout.
Optimization treated as bounded discrete experiments logged to results.tsv with PASS/FAIL and explicit budget counting toward the ≤8 limit (level-8 trait).

Optimization was reactive try/measure/revert with variance confusion and hung/cancelled compiles rather than a pre-planned risk-ordered hypothesis search; no explicit per-method parity milestones — keeps it short of level 8-10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly sequenced implement-API → verify parity → freeze model.py → optimize a copy, with the correctness checkpoint robustly protected via repeated reverts and the shim pointing at the optimized file, satisfying the level-5 anchor fully. It further treated optimization as bounded, scoped, budget-counted discrete experiments logged in results.tsv — a level-8 trait — but did not establish explicit per-method parity milestones and pursued the ≤8 experiments reactively rather than as a pre-planned risk-ordered hypothesis search (level 10). This places observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 7.

dimensions.name: Designing parity and latency checks

evidence.note: Analyzed benchmark harness tolerances (atol=5e-4, rtol=1e-3), found sample diff exceeded tolerance, diagnosed TF32 matmul as the cause of numerical divergence and disabled it — tolerance-aware parity reasoning against the reference, beyond mere latency.
Introspected the JAX param tree before writing model.py to get layer naming/shapes right, but did not construct a standalone per-layer numerical comparison harness against JAX.

Re-ran benchmark.py after each optimization and recorded PASS/FAIL in results.tsv; caught a FAIL_REGRESSION at step 87 and reverted — re-checks output equivalence via the harness after every experiment, not just latency.
Final verification was a single benchmark.py run confirming PASS + latency; no independent cross-check that PASS reflects true per-method parity.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent compares PyTorch outputs against the reference for the main loss/sample paths and consistently uses benchmark.py to check latency and PASS/FAIL after every optimization (level 5), and adds real rigor by diagnosing a TF32 parity bug via tolerance analysis and catching a regression at step 87. But it never builds its own layer-level/per-method parity checks (embed_prefix/embed_suffix/forward/sample_actions) with explicit tolerances or seeded determinism verification, relying entirely on the provided harness — so it falls short of the level-8 anchor. This places it at a 6, above the pure main-path level 5 but well below a self-built verification harness.

dimensions.name: Tracking parity status and experiment budget

evidence.note: Each optimization experiment appended to results.tsv with baseline_ms, latency_ms, improvement_pct, status (PASS/FAIL_REGRESSION) and a note describing the approach — a genuine per-experiment ledger, not an afterthought.
Explicitly tracks experiment budget against the ≤8 cap ('used 6 experiments counting baseline', later 'used 8 experiments'), showing live awareness of remaining slots.

Detected a regression (12.82ms worse than incumbent 10.06ms), correctly identified the previous best config, and reverted to it (9.13ms) — consistently knows the current fastest-passing variant without re-deriving.

Benchmark variance muddied the ledger: a 'rerun confirms compile config' recorded as 16.4ms improvement over 19.5ms, and near-noise 16.4→16.9 comparisons; several reruns of equivalent configs consumed attention, short of the waste-avoiding reconciliation of level 10.
Final rewrite of autoresearch_logs.md summarizing the experiment trail, tying the arc together at completion.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent kept an accurate running ledger in results.tsv tying each experiment to a hypothesis note, latency, parity status, and explicitly tracked budget consumption against the ≤8 cap, and it reliably identified and reverted to the incumbent fastest-passing variant (steps 87-88) — squarely anchor-8 behavior. It falls short of 10 because benchmark variance led to recording reruns of equivalent configurations as if they were new progress and to slightly loose experiment counting, rather than a fully waste-avoiding, continuously reconciled allocation of the last budget slots.

dimensions.name: Responding to parity failures and unproductive optimizations

evidence.note: Sample-parity failure diagnosed to root cause (TF32 matmul precision), disabled TF32, and fixed a self-introduced __future__ import ordering bug — targeted correction of numerical divergence.
SDPA (61.5ms) and buffer (65.7ms) optimizations regressed; reverted both cleanly with reasoned explanations rather than pressing on.

torch.compile CUDAGraph tensor-reuse issue and max-autotune/reduce-overhead hangs; cancelled and reverted to frozen model.py checkpoint each time, then switched compile modes based on the specific failure cause.

After reaching 10.05ms PASS, a further compile change regressed to 12.82ms logged as FAIL_REGRESSION; reverted to the 9.13ms PASS variant, ending on a defensibly chosen fastest-passing implementation, not the last thing tried.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent treated failures as diagnostic signals: it isolated the parity failure to TF32, reverted every optimization that regressed correctness or latency cleanly back to the frozen model.py, and abandoned hanging/unpromising directions quickly to conserve budget. It redirected effort toward the kernel-overhead hypothesis (torch.compile/CUDA graphs) and ended by explicitly rejecting a FAIL_REGRESSION in favor of the fastest passing variant — squarely matching the level-8 anchor, with only loose noise-attribution keeping it below a perfect 10.

dimensions.name: Budget-bounded optimization discipline

evidence.note: Opened optimization with distinct, differentiated early hypotheses (remove .item() host sync, SDPA attention, precompute prefix mask buffers), each benchmarked and each explicitly kept-or-reverted based on measured result — showing hypothesis-driven trials rather than random tinkering.

Sequenced increasingly higher-payoff ideas informed by prior results: torch.compile default (46.99%), extend compile to more submodules/full forward (55-58%), then reduce-overhead cudagraphs (78%). Reasoned about the actual bottleneck (kernel-launch overhead on a tiny model) to motivate the compile/cudagraph direction.

Explicitly tracked budget ('We've used 6 experiments (counting baseline)' at 85; 'We have used 8 experiments' at 88), honored the ≤8 cap, and after a regression (12.82ms FAIL_REGRESSION) reverted to the fastest passing checkpoint (9.13ms/80.48%) as the final submission.

Several attempts (max-autotune, reduce-overhead cudagraph, compile sample_actions) hung and were cancelled; these muddy the experiment count and the 'counting baseline' bookkeeping is loose, and confirmation reruns (step 73) were also logged as results, keeping this short of a clean, precise budget accounting.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent treated the 8-experiment cap as a real constraint: it logged distinct, hypothesis-driven attempts to results.tsv, sequenced them from higher expected payoff (compile → broader compile → cudagraphs) with each choice informed by the previous result, and stopped cleanly at the cap by reverting to the fastest passing implementation. This exceeds the level-5 anchor (within budget, distinct experiments, fastest passing selected) and reaches into level-8 territory of deliberate allocation across genuinely different hypotheses. It falls short of a clean 8/10 because the budget accounting is loose — several aborted/hung runs and confirmation reruns blur the count and the 'counting baseline' logic is imprecise — so a 7 best fits.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon, two-phase engineering task: first faithfully port an under-documented renamed JAX policy to PyTorch behind a precise API contract (many named symbols/methods, deterministic behavior, numerical parity), then produce an optimized inference variant that preserves outputs while beating a latency gate. Difficulty comes from reverse-engineering JAX semantics for exact parity, a rigid interface surface, a hard budget (≤8 optimization experiments, keep fastest passing), and required experiment bookkeeping. A skilled practitioner invests heavily in orientation and verification, sequences correctness-before-speed strictly, and manages the experiment budget deliberately.

dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the JAX source & API contract
dimensions.description: Reading and understanding the existing JAX policy, its config, and the exact required PyTorch API surface before and while writing code.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Numerical parity and topology compatibility are impossible without precisely understanding the JAX implementation's layer shapes, init, flow (embed_prefix/suffix, sampling loop), and the specified symbol/method contract; acting blind guarantees rework.

anchors.0: Starts writing model.py without reading the JAX source or the config; invents an architecture.
anchors.3: Skims the JAX file and copies obvious layers, but never maps out the full forward/sample flow or the required symbol list, missing methods or misreading shapes.
anchors.5: Reads the JAX policy and config, enumerates the required symbols/methods (CharizardTorchModel, PokeTree, throw_pokeball, evolve_charizard, embed_prefix/suffix, sample_actions, PokemonCenter.img/llm), and understands the main data flow before coding.
anchors.8: Systematically traces each JAX module to its intended PyTorch equivalent — parameter layouts, init, dtype/device handling, the noise/time/timestep semantics and sampling loop — and records assumptions about ambiguous points, distinguishing the actual JAX contract from any public-project prior.
anchors.10: Builds a precise, evidence-backed mental model of the entire policy: derives exact tensor shapes and numerical conventions (weight transposition, normalization, RNG/noise ordering) from the JAX source, anticipates parity pitfalls (e.g. layout differences, default configs), and revisits the source to resolve discrepancies as they surface during implementation.

dimensions.name: Sequencing correctness-then-optimization into checkpointed milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into an ordered hierarchy — build each API piece, achieve parity, freeze model.py, then run bounded optimization experiments — each with a clear done-condition.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task has an explicit phase gate (correct model.py must be preserved as checkpoint before optimizing a copy) and a scoring split across topology/parity/latency; treating it as one push risks optimizing before correctness or corrupting the checkpoint.

anchors.0: No structure; edits everything at once, mixes optimization into model.py, no notion of phase gate.
anchors.3: Vague two-step intent but no explicit milestones or done-criteria; may begin optimizing before parity is established.
anchors.5: Clear phases: implement full API, verify parity, copy to model_optimized.py, then optimize — with the correctness checkpoint respected and the shim pointed at the optimized file.
anchors.8: Milestones are explicit and independently checkable (per-method parity, end-to-end loss/sampling parity, checkpoint frozen, each optimization experiment scoped), with optimization treated as a bounded sequence of discrete experiments rather than open-ended tinkering.
anchors.10: A disciplined milestone hierarchy that orders by risk (hardest-to-parity components first), defines the exact done-signal for each, protects the frozen checkpoint, and plans the ≤8 optimization experiments as a coherent search (what hypothesis each tests) before spending the budget.

dimensions.name: Designing parity and latency checks
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks for topology, layer-level numerical parity, end-to-end loss/sampling parity, and using the benchmark harness to confirm latency gains and preserved outputs.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The submission is scored precisely on these parities and the latency gate; without self-built numerical comparisons against the JAX reference and disciplined use of benchmark.py, the agent cannot know it succeeded and optimizations may silently change outputs.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes port is correct and that optimizations preserve outputs without checking.
anchors.3: Runs the model once to see it doesn't crash, or runs benchmark.py only for latency, with no numerical comparison to the JAX reference.
anchors.5: Compares PyTorch outputs against the JAX reference for the main forward/sample paths and uses benchmark.py to check latency and PASS/FAIL after optimization.
anchors.8: Builds layer-level / per-method parity checks (embed_prefix, embed_suffix, forward, sample_actions) with explicit tolerances, verifies determinism given fixed noise/time, and after every optimization re-checks output equivalence against the frozen model.py — not just the latency number.
anchors.10: A rigorous verification harness: systematic numerical comparison across components and end-to-end (loss and sampling) with sensible tolerances and seeded RNG, guards that catch subtle divergence introduced by each optimization, and cross-checks that benchmark.py's PASS status reflects true output parity rather than being gamed — verification designed before results are trusted.

dimensions.name: Tracking parity status and experiment budget
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which API pieces pass parity, which experiments have run against the ≤8 budget, and which is the current fastest passing implementation.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With a hard experiment cap, a required experiment trail (results.tsv, autoresearch_logs.md), and a 'keep the fastest passing' rule, losing track of what's done, what passed, and what's best leads to wasted budget or shipping a worse variant.

anchors.0: No tracking; doesn't know how many experiments have run, which passed, or which is fastest; trail files empty or absent.
anchors.3: Sparse notes; loses count of experiments or forgets which variant currently wins; trail is an afterthought.
anchors.5: Maintains results.tsv and autoresearch_logs.md with baseline/latency/status per experiment and knows the current best passing variant and remaining budget.
anchors.8: Keeps an accurate running ledger tying each experiment to its hypothesis, latency, parity status, and budget consumed; consistently identifies the incumbent fastest-passing implementation and remaining parity gaps without re-deriving them.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles done-vs-remaining across both phases: detects when an optimization thread is unproductive early, avoids re-running equivalent experiments, and uses the trail as a live decision instrument to allocate the last few budget slots to the highest-value ideas.

dimensions.name: Responding to parity failures and unproductive optimizations
dimensions.description: Revising approach when numerical parity fails, when an optimization breaks outputs, or when a latency experiment fails to improve — rather than pressing on.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Porting will surface parity mismatches and optimizations that regress correctness or don't help; with a capped budget, the agent must diagnose root causes and change course instead of burning experiments on a falsified approach.

anchors.0: Ignores failing parity or FAIL status; keeps the broken variant or barrels ahead on a falsified assumption.
anchors.3: Notices failures but responds with random tweaks rather than diagnosis; may keep a non-passing variant or abandon parity.
anchors.5: When parity or a benchmark fails, investigates the cause and adjusts (fixes layout/init, reverts a bad optimization, discards non-passing variants to keep the fastest passing one).
anchors.8: Diagnoses divergence to its root (e.g. a specific layer's numerics, RNG ordering, dtype) and makes targeted corrections; abandons unpromising optimization directions quickly to conserve budget and reverts cleanly to the frozen checkpoint when needed.
anchors.10: Treats each failure as evidence that updates the plan: isolates root causes systematically, redirects the remaining experiment budget toward hypotheses the failures point to, and ends with a defensibly chosen fastest-passing implementation rather than the last thing tried.

dimensions.name: Budget-bounded optimization discipline
dimensions.description: Treating the ≤8 optimization experiments as a scarce resource allocated across distinct, hypothesis-driven attempts, and honoring the stop condition.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task explicitly caps experiments and requires stopping with the fastest passing implementation; undisciplined trial-and-error either exhausts the budget prematurely or overruns it, and is a meta-work demand beyond generic monitoring.

anchors.0: Ignores the cap entirely — either endless tinkering or no real optimization attempts, no notion of a stop rule.
anchors.3: Runs optimizations ad hoc with little differentiation between attempts and loose regard for the 8-experiment limit.
anchors.5: Stays within the budget, keeps distinct experiments, and stops with a passing implementation selected as fastest.
anchors.8: Allocates the budget deliberately across genuinely different optimization hypotheses, sequences them from highest expected payoff, and stops cleanly once diminishing returns or the cap is reached.
anchors.10: Runs a near-optimal search under the constraint: each experiment tests a distinct, well-motivated idea informed by prior results, redundant attempts are avoided, and the final choice is justified as the best latency-vs-parity trade-off within the spent budget.
